sources.title: Sternicza neighbourhood expansion
sources.details: 124 additional source footprints within 200 m nearest-footprint distance, processed 2026-11-13; official LoD1 ALS median heights, descriptive direction labels, and a retained source extract. The original site, buildings and analytical terrain are preserved. See data/sternicza-neighborhood-source.json.

limitations: Includes parcel 400 behind parcel 401; cadastral geometry does not verify ownership.
House floor (+1.2 m), eye levels, glazing, terrace, canopy and landscape are adjustable design assumptions, not a measured building survey.
Five apartment volumes are sampled. Coverage means blocked sample rays from one selected observer, not area percentage or a whole-garden privacy guarantee.
Hedges are ideal continuous opaque screens, not porous or tapered individual plants. Existing vegetation is not modelled.
PCK 3 returns above absolute elevation 24 m are isolated thin features of unconfirmed identity and excluded unless high features are enabled.
Farther blocks use median LoD1 roofs; their roof objects and true maxima may be higher.

The mapped own-house body blocks sightlines from outdoor observers. Indoor presets assume an open sightline through glazing; individual walls, window apertures and existing tree crowns are not surveyed analytical obstructions. Nearby mapped buildings are approximate flat-roof blockers.
Moving garden grade does not move the house floor. Existing hedge tops remain fixed when new planting is disabled.
A raised garden is a geometry experiment, not drainage, foundation or retaining-wall approval.

Expanded neighbourhood context uses 2024 source footprints and approximate LoD1 median roof bodies. Labels describe directions and distances, not verified postal addresses or current building condition. The separate 4 m surrounding terrain is for rendering only; the original analytical terrain remains unchanged.

sources.title: Cellar plan
sources.reading: 900 cm depth, 40 cm outer walls, 440 / 40 / 340 cm internal depth chain. Brick-floored corridor and four earth-floored cellar rooms. Rear external access and separate internal stair.

sources.title: Ground-floor plan
sources.reading: 1077 cm overall, a centred 355 cm entrance bay, paired street stairs and granite posts. Two board-floored rear rooms, two kitchens, hall and bathroom. Note to straighten the lower flight of the existing timber stair.

sources.title: First-floor plan
sources.reading: Three rear rooms, cranked master partition, hall, large front room including bay, kitchen, bathroom, 80 × 200 cm doors and folding attic stair. Rear room widths 420, 342, 240 cm. The bay is 307 × 168 cm internally; its 355 cm masonry width has 10 cm external insulation on each side. Two rear windows on this sheet.

sources.title: Section I–I
sources.reading: −2.50 m foundation line, −2.00 cellar floor, ±0.00 ground floor, +3.05 first floor, +5.75 upper ceiling, +8.75 ridge and +9.60 chimney. Clear spaces 1.70, 2.75 and 2.70 m. Roof marked 30°. Local +7.25 m reference.

sources.title: Street elevation
sources.reading: Central projecting gable and bay, two flanking flights, multipane joinery, ground-floor shutters, plinth, eaves and two chimney stacks. The central lower panels differ from the openings on other sheets.

sources.title: Side elevation
sources.reading: Paired side windows at each occupied level, two small cellar lights and a circular gable vent. The projecting front bay has a narrow upper side light.

sources.title: Separate garage or outbuilding elevations
sources.reading: North elevation has two portals beneath a pitched roof. West has a side door, window and dormer. South gable and east wall are shown largely blank. No dimensioned floor plan.

sources.title: Floor structure over ground floor, 1:50
sources.reading: Existing timber floors, reinforced concrete ring beams W, concrete B15 and steel A0. Stair opening, front projection and 361 / 355 / 361 cm frontage chain. References to structural sheets 3/K and 6/K.

sources.title: Ground-floor renovation markup
sources.reading: Open kitchen and living space, large dining table, U-shaped seating and right-wall TV, combined bathroom, broad rear HST and 4 m terrace.

sources.title: First-floor renovation markup
sources.reading: Expanded master, office, three guest bedrooms, wardrobe, compact sauna, whirlpool, soaking tub and two-person shower. A shared 4 m balcony extends across all three rear rooms. The later bathroom brief supersedes the two-tub markup: one hydrotherapy spa upstairs, with the deep soaking tub downstairs.

ground: Open the partition between the rear rooms and the wall between dining and the front-left kitchen. Keep the two flue cores visible.
Join the right kitchen and bathroom. Keep access through the landing and remove the redundant internal doorway with the divider.
Fit one deep soaking tub, a walk-in shower, a dual vanity, WC and bidet. Put the mirror on the solid stair wall and keep the low bidet below the street-window sill.
Provide near-full-width rear lift-and-slide glazing (HST) to the 4.00 m terrace.
Place a long table on the left, U-shaped seating facing a right-wall TV, and fitted cabinets in the front-left kitchen.
first: Straighten the master bedroom’s stepped front partition. Retain the middle office and right guest bedroom.
Divide the front-left room into guest bedrooms II and III, with a new side corridor and independent doors. Enclose the bay as a wardrobe.
Combine the kitchen and bath into a spa bathroom with one large hydrotherapy tub, jets and lighting, a two-person shower, a single vanity and WC.

Enclose the right end of the hall for the sauna and move its new bath partition 0.36 m to give about 1.28 × 1.30 m clear. Move the guest-room door left and hinge the sauna door to open outward along the hall’s lower edge.
Open three separate rear doors onto one continuous 4.00 m shared balcony.
basement: Keep the drawn cellar as the baseline. The optional two-car conversion compares a lowered floor and two straight parking lanes against its stair and chimney cores.
The street entry and large garage aperture need their own structural design. Existing cellar access below the proposed rear terrace also needs coordination.
attic: Retain a single unpartitioned roof space, exposed truss envelope and folding access. No conversion into bedrooms is marked.

registration.note: Inside and outside use one 10.77 × 9.00 m drawing-based house, including its front bay. The model is centred on the surveyed street wall without scaling. The archived drawings and current photograph differ; exact registration and present-day alterations still need an as-built survey.

interiors.note: Drawing reconstruction and annotated renovation proposal. The photographs may predate the current house; geometry, structural removals and equipment loads require verification.

optimization.method: bounded parabolic-transition search; two orientations, refined final sweep

assessment.assessmentScope: Closed-car ramp geometry only; existing cellar structure is assessed separately.
warnings: The supplied historical section shows a cellar floor at −2.00 m, 0.30 m ground-floor structure and 1.70 m clear height. Present conditions, foundations, drainage and vehicle bumper geometry still need measurement.
The entire underside is conservatively flat at the selected level-road clearance, including both overhangs; tyre radii are nominal size geometry.
Quasi-static rigid-body geometry excludes braking, suspension travel, tyre deflection, snow, ruts and construction tolerances.
The road approach and crossing are assumed flush and level. The required drainage/containment threshold detail is unresolved; a 30 mm edge is not included.
The 25% gradient, 3 m access width and 2.20 m structural headroom figures are transitional design benchmarks; project applicability needs confirmation.
The 2.10 m door opening is an assumption without surveyed lintel or door-gear geometry; overhead checks use a conservative full-height closed-car envelope.

The two-car plan uses two Cyberster envelopes, each 4.535 m long, 1.913 m wide at the body and 2.110 m across its mirrors. The comparison assumes closed doors. Door opening and street turning manoeuvres remain unverified.

Parking width is compared with a chosen 0.30 m mirror-to-wall allowance and, for two cars, 0.60 m between mirror envelopes. These are planning allowances, not a surveyed door-opening or accessibility assessment.

The wider ramp requires proposed side-return entry stairs and a 1.0 m cantilevered landing at the existing front door. Its 0.18 m slab underside is included in both driving sweeps; its structure has not been designed.

The straight two-car approach conflicts with retained stairs / chimney structure in the supplied basement plan. The clearance sweep does not remove these obstructions or establish a viable conversion.
The proposed floor is 0.60 m below the documented cellar floor; foundation and structural design are unresolved.
The bottom curve continues inside the existing house and requires structural and basement-layout design.

basementGarage.note: Conditional geometric comparison using an assumed flat underside and design reserve. Survey, structure, drainage, traction, local rules, headroom and door-opening envelopes remain separate checks.

assumptions: A canopy post moves sideways along the front edge to clear the jacuzzi service band. The beam extension, connection and footing are proposed.
The canopy is a roof proposal, without an occupiable floor or guardrail. Its height is measured above the living terrace.

rows.label: Custom overflow jacuzzi · installed
rows.scope: Full custom overflow spa, structure, balance tank, hydraulics and installation allowance. No supplier quote; not a certified modification of Vienna Life.

rows.label: Six-person sauna · installed
rows.scope: Cabin, heater, glazing, insulated base, access steps, delivery, local electrical connection and installation. Custom diagonal glazing needs its own offer.

rows.label: Cold plunge · installed
rows.scope: Plunge shell, chiller, pad, steps, local water/electric connections and installation. The catalog product is smaller; this is a custom-feature allowance.

rows.label: Sunken fire lounge · installed
rows.scope: Excavation and disposal, retaining structure, waterproofing, drainage, built-in seats and cushions, burner and fuel installation. Burner reference is net; the full planning range aims to include tax.

rows.label: Raised terrace, finish and steps
rows.scope: Raised terrace frame, waterproofing, finish, removable spa service hatches and garden steps. Jacuzzi support is in the spa line; house facade / doors are excluded.

rows.label: Paths and dining paving
rows.scope: Dining pad plus a 1.15 m path with 90% stone coverage. Finish and local sub-base; excludes pool coping, terrace, access stairs and spa foundations.

rows.label: Dining set and loungers
rows.basis: 1 dining set (6 seats) + 2 loungers + delivery / handling allowance
rows.scope: Movable furniture only. Built-in lounge seats/cushions are in the fire-lounge line. The named Cloveris benchmarks advertise free delivery; the generic range reserves 500–1,500 PLN for alternative delivery or placement assistance. Product references are not additional costs.

rows.label: Ornamental planting
rows.scope: Assume 20% of garden left after hedge beds and paving. Ornamental plants, mulch and planting labour; excludes thujas, specimen trees and added bulk topsoil.

rows.label: Lawn finish
rows.scope: Lawn finish and fine grading on prepared soil. No additional bulk fill or topsoil charged here.

rows.label: Permanent garden irrigation
rows.basis: 326.3 m² irrigation basis × 35–65 PLN/m² · includes 11.5 m² front-hedge strip + 35.2 m² front-side hedge strips
rows.scope: Permanent distribution, controls and installation for beds, hedges and lawn. Street and front-side hedges use a provisional 1 m planted-strip width for drip irrigation only; no front lawn or fill. Specimen establishment visits / temporary root-ball watering are separate.

rows.label: Landscape lighting
rows.basis: 39 fittings: 12 baseline + 3 garden pendants + 24 hedge lanterns · generic 700–1,500 PLN each installed
rows.scope: Existing generic lighting allowance applied to the illustrated fittings, local wiring and simple mounts; no pendant product or support-frame quotation has been received. Replace with a complete installed quote covering the selected shades, posts, foundations and controls. Switching a light off does not remove its installation cost. Spa built-in lights belong to their object lines; the main supply is in shared utilities.

rows.label: Shared garden utilities
rows.scope: Shared garden electric and water feeds, distribution and drain connections only. Object-level hookups and garden-fill drainage are excluded here to avoid duplication.

rows.label: Garden design and coordination
rows.scope: Garden design, level coordination and structural / services coordination allowances, including the selected full perimeter hedges. House renovation, first-floor balcony, basement garage, new gates / fencing and main utility upgrades are outside these garden allowances.

rows.label: Detached garage removal
rows.scope: Allowance for removal of the detached garage and its waste transport/disposal. Final demolition method and quantities require a site quote. No separate duplicate general-waste charge.

rows.label: Terrace canopy
rows.scope: Selected terrace canopy, supports and installation; not charged when the cover is disabled or replaced with a balcony.

rows.label: Basement garage + ramp · full installed quote
rows.basis: Two-car basement conversion and full front-yard approach
rows.scope: Survey, design, structural opening and alterations, excavation/disposal, retaining walls, waterproofing, drainage/pumping, garage door, services, ramp finish and proposed gate relocation. Confirm the entire scope and applicable tax; the garden budget does not price these works.

notes: Stock height does not guarantee an opaque hedge. Spacing and crown width must be checked with the nursery.

Front / street thujas are counted separately on each planted span; proposed pedestrian and vehicle openings are excluded. The street hedge follows original ground, with no front-garden fill or raised-bed charge. New gates, fencing and driveway construction are excluded.

Left and right thujas extend along the full mapped plot edges. Their front-side sections stay at original grade and add plant supply, planting labour and drip irrigation only; no front-side garden fill or raised beds are charged. Hedge delivery remains one allowance for the whole order.
Earthwork excludes garage demolition, excavated-pool soil reuse, topsoil stripping/disposal, new paving and professional design. Retaining, drainage, transport and access are editable allowances.

Installed spa ranges are planning assumptions, supported by separate product references. They include each object’s foundations, local connections and commissioning. They are not supplier quotations for this site.
The basement garage and front ramp need a complete project quote. Zero means unquoted and excluded from the known subtotal; garden retaining/drainage allowances do not include basement works.

Garden allowances cover the rear garden + full perimeter hedges: terrace, spa programme, planting, site works and selected garage removal / canopy. Property purchase, house renovation, first-floor balcony, basement garage, front driveway, gates / fencing, operating bills and major utility-capacity upgrades are excluded from these garden allowances. The selected basement garage and ramp use the separate project quote above.

No double charge for hedge/specimen supply, garden-fill drainage/retaining or spa foundations in garden finishes. Pool coping and built-in lounge seats belong to their spa lines. Terrace finish excludes the jacuzzi footprint. Ordinary paths and lawn need finish only, with bulk fill accounted separately.

Planning rates are explicit design assumptions, not surveyed contractor rates. Ranges aim to include applicable tax, but published references retain their own gross/net/unspecified tax labels. No supplier has provided a site-specific offer; replace whole-line allowances with confirmed installed gross quotations.

Screening-tree prices describe purchased specimens, not mature sizes or guaranteed available stock. Only enabled trees are included. Latest catalog review: 2026-11-14; individual entries retain their observation dates. Crown shape and density still need specimen confirmation.
Some selected specimen prices do not state their VAT basis. Enter final tax-inclusive supplier quotes before purchasing.

sunlight.method: Direct-sun visibility at 1 m outdoor sample centres, using mapped building bodies and sampled roofs, fixed house/garage roof elevations, local terrain, opaque hedges, the proposed canopy and valid enabled screening trees with seasonal crown geometry. Optional pergola members, explicitly assumed dense established foliage and finite spa screens use the same geometry as privacy rays. Water uses matched levels and excavated openings. The spa proposal adds opaque sauna walls/roof with transparent glazing, cold-plunge rim and steps, and a lowered lounge floor with retaining walls, steps and fixed seating. The sauna interior is excluded from outdoor area.
sunlight.limitations: No weather, diffuse/reflected light, glass transmission losses, existing tree crowns, decorative planting/movable furniture, isolated unverified high roof returns, or terrain beyond the supplied DTM. Samples approximate surface area; small spa zones have few samples. Roof interpolation, missing-roof fallbacks and foliage permeability remain simplified.

garage.note: A sampled planning model, not a survey, sunlight-hours study or whole-property privacy guarantee.

balcony.summary: 8.5 × 4.0 m · 34.0 m² proposed first-floor balcony. Finished deck +3.05 m above the terrace; 2.80 m below the slab and 2.56 m below the front beam. 1.10 m clear-glass guard; Current retains the original first-floor windows; choose a renovation style to add balcony access. Floor height follows the first-floor assumption. Structure, foundations, waterproofing and drainage require project design and a separate quote.
